successCriteria.description: The LeaveRequest entity and the three DTOs (CreateLeaveRequestDto, UpdateLeaveRequestDto, LeaveRequestQueryParams) are exported from the leave model with the canonical type shapes: status typed as LeaveStatus, approvedBy as string|null, approvedAt as Date|null, reason as string|undefined.

createLeaveRequestSchema rejects input that is missing required fields, contains non-ISO date strings, or has startDate >= endDate; it accepts input with all required fields, valid ISO dates, and startDate < endDate.
updateLeaveRequestSchema rejects non-ISO date strings and rejects startDate >= endDate when both dates are present; it accepts valid partial input (any subset of optional fields) and empty input.
Repository.create persists a row via INSERT with NOW(), NOW() timestamps and RETURNING *, and returns the mapped camelCase LeaveRequest entity (not the raw snake_case row).
Repository.findById returns the mapped LeaveRequest entity when a row matches and returns null when no row matches.

Repository.findByEmployee applies each supplied queryParams field (status, leaveTypeId, startDateFrom/To, endDateFrom/To, limit, offset) as a dynamic WHERE/limit clause using parameterised placeholders, and omits undefined fields.

Repository.findByApprover resolves the approver's queue by joining the employees table on manager_id (not by filtering approved_by), so pending/SUBMITTED requests whose approved_by is null are returned for the approver's direct reports; supplied queryParams are applied as additional conditions on the joined query.
Repository.updateStatus sets the status column, sets approved_by and approved_at when supplied, appends updated_at = NOW(), and returns the updated entity or null when no row matches.

Repository.update applies only the supplied mutable fields (startDate, endDate, reason) via a dynamic SET clause, appends updated_at = NOW(), and falls back to findById when no mutable fields are supplied.
The leave barrel (index.ts) re-exports the model types, the repository interface and class, and the validation schemas; it does not export service/controller/routes (those are later phases).

Unit tests cover found, not-found, empty-result, and database-error cases for every repository method, asserting exact SQL via toHaveBeenCalledWith / stringContaining; validation tests cover valid and each invalid-input case.
No `any` type appears anywhere in the leave module source; repository query parameter arrays are typed as unknown[] with type guards/casts at the mapping boundary.

constraints: All database access in the leave module must go through the LeaveRepository class using the shared pool (GP-001); no inline SQL or direct pool usage outside the repository.
No `any` type is permitted; use `unknown` with type guards/casts at the row-mapping boundary (HARNESS no-any rule, severity high).
Modules import each other only through their declared index.ts barrel; the leave module imports shared types via ../../shared/types/index and the db pool via ../../shared/db/connection.
All SQL must use parameterised $N placeholders with incremental paramIndex; no string-interpolated user values in queries.

Test files must be named *.test.ts under tests/ and import via path aliases rooted at src (jest moduleDirectories: ['node_modules', 'src']); the pool must be mocked via jest.mock('shared/db/connection', () => ({ pool: { query: jest.fn() } })).

The LeaveRequest entity uses camelCase fields and does not extend BaseEntity (which is snake_case); the repository maps between snake_case DB rows and camelCase entities via a private Row type and mapRow function.
Zod schemas must be imported from the canonical 'zod' entry point (package.json lists zod@^4.4.3); this is the first validation file in the repo so no in-repo pattern exists to copy.
outOfScope: LeaveService and its business rules (submit/approve/reject/cancel orchestration, balance deduction, overlap detection, minimum-notice enforcement, auto-approval) — Phase 8.
LeaveController and leave.routes.ts (HTTP translation, RBAC enforcement, request.user consumption) — Phase 9.
Audit record writing for leave state changes (GP-002) — the repository does not write audit records; that is the service layer's responsibility in Phase 8.
RBAC enforcement on repository methods — the repository is unauthenticated data access; authorization is enforced in the service/controller layers (Phases 8–9).
Validation schemas for approve/reject/cancel/query operations — Phase 7 only requires createLeaveRequestSchema and updateLeaveRequestSchema.
Custom error classes (InsufficientBalanceError, ApproverNotAuthorizedError, LeaveRequestNotFoundError, InvalidStateTransitionError) — Phase 8.

entityInvariants.invariant: A LeaveRequest's status is always one of the LeaveStatus enum values (DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED); the repository never persists or returns an out-of-enum status string.
A LeaveRequest's endDate is strictly greater than its startDate; the validation schemas enforce this and the repository persists the dates as supplied without reordering them.
approvedBy and approvedAt are nullable and are null while the request is in DRAFT/SUBMITTED status; they are populated only when the request transitions to APPROVED or REJECTED via updateStatus.

createdAt and updatedAt are set by the database (NOW()) on insert and updatedAt is refreshed on every update; the repository never accepts or persists caller-supplied timestamp values for these fields.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns null when no row matches; propagates database errors as rejected promises.
Returns an empty array when no rows match; propagates database errors as rejected promises.
Returns an empty array when the approver has no matching direct-report requests; propagates database errors as rejected promises.
Returns the persisted entity; propagates constraint violations (e.g. duplicate key, FK violations) as rejected promises.
Returns the updated entity or null when no row matches; propagates database errors as rejected promises.
Returns the updated entity, the existing entity when no mutable fields are supplied, or null when no row matches; propagates database errors as rejected promises.
Rejects missing required fields, non-ISO dates, and startDate >= endDate with a typed Zod error; accepts valid input and produces a typed output object.
Rejects non-ISO dates and startDate >= endDate (when both present) with a typed Zod error; accepts valid partial or empty input.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The LeaveRepository must replicate the established repository pattern: co-located ILeaveRepository interface + LeaveRepository class + private snake_case Row type + mapRowToLeaveRequest function; parameterised $N placeholders with incremental paramIndex; dynamic SET/WHERE via conditions[]/params[] arrays; create() uses INSERT ... NOW(), NOW() RETURNING *; update() builds dynamic SET from mutableFields + appends updated_at = NOW() + falls back to findById.

The LeaveRequest.status field and the validation schemas must use the LeaveStatus enum (DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED) imported from the canonical shared types; the repository must cast the snake_case status column back to LeaveStatus at the mapping boundary.

The findByApprover query must join the employees table on manager_id to resolve the approver's direct reports, consistent with the Employee entity's managerId field being the approval-routing key (approved_by is null for pending requests and cannot be used to find a manager's queue).

The leave barrel (index.ts) must follow the sibling barrel convention: re-export model types, repository interface + class, and validation schemas; downstream modules are consumed only through barrels in later phases.

The leave repository and validation tests must follow the established test conventions: jest.mock('shared/db/connection', () => ({ pool: { query: jest.fn() } })), makeRow()/makeEntity() factory helpers with overrides, beforeEach mock reset, exact-SQL assertions via toHaveBeenCalledWith and stringContaining, and found/not-found/empty/error coverage per method.

The leave_requests table column set (id, employee_id, leave_type_id, start_date, end_date, reason, status, approved_by, approved_at, created_at, updated_at) in the reconciled schema must be the exact set the repository reads and writes; no extra columns and no omitted columns.

integrationPoints.why: LeaveRequest.status is typed as LeaveStatus; the model imports LeaveStatus from the canonical shared types.
LeaveRepository is the sole pool consumer in the leave module (GP-001); it imports the shared pool for all queries.
findByApprover joins the employees table on manager_id to resolve the approver's direct reports; the Employee entity's managerId field is the approval-routing key.

LeaveRequest.leaveTypeId references a LeavePolicy; the model/DTO type for leaveTypeId is consistent with the policy id type (string). Phase 7 only declares the type relationship; the service resolves it in Phase 8.
Declared as a Phase 7 dependency for context; the repository does not call it (audit writing is the service layer's job in Phase 8), but the leave module's later service will consume IAuditService.

Declared as a Phase 7 dependency for context; the repository does not call it (balance deduction/restoration is the service layer's job in Phase 8), but the leave module's later service will consume IBalanceService.
